# [TASK] Drop the markdown child lists; native sub-issues own hierarchy

## Task
Make GitHub's native sub-issue link the only record of parent-to-child
hierarchy. The `## Child Stories` and `## Technical Tasks` markdown lists
duplicate it and are maintained by hand on every edit.

The lists carry nothing native does not. A markdown label is the child's
title with the `[STORY] As a <role>, I want` prefix removed, and the
checkbox is the child's open/closed state, which GitHub already tracks.

Measured before the change: 52 parents, 0 membership mismatches, 1 wrong
checkbox. #77 was closed with `- [x] #120` ticked while #120 is open, which
hid an open Task under a closed Story.

As of this Task, the child's own `## Parent Epic` / `## Parent Story` line
stayed, holding an explicit "no parent, because ..." decision that native
linkage cannot express. #253 later removed that line entirely; see Notes.

## No parent
No parent. Backlog convention change with no user-facing slice. Follows the
same reasoning as #253, which removes `## Sprint` because the milestone
field owns it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The epic template has no `## Child Stories` section and the
      user-story template no `## Technical Tasks` section
- [x] Both templates state that closure is blocked by an open sub-issue,
      replacing the "unchecked box" rule the lists carried
      (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/epic.md`'s "Closing this Epic" section and
      `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/user-story.md`'s "Closing this Story"
      section)
- [x] No issue on the board carries a `## Child Stories` or
      `## Technical Tasks` section (`grep -rl '^## Child Stories\|^##
      Technical Tasks' .github/issues/backlog/` returns nothing)
- [x] `AGENTS.md` describes hierarchy as the native sub-issue link only,
      with a `## No parent` section for the explicit no-parent case
- [x] The git mirror header lists each issue's children
      (`.github/issues/backlog/<n>.md`'s `children:` field, e.g.
      `.github/issues/backlog/316.md`)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 3

## Notes
#77 is being reopened separately. It is closed with an open child Task
(#120), which the cascading-closure rule does not allow.

Audited by #317: #253 (issue templates rewritten to the audit standard)
superseded the explicit `## Parent Epic` / `## Parent Story` line this
Task shipped. The current design carries only the native sub-issue link,
plus `## No parent` for the case where none exists.
